items.title: 2.2 Effect of an electric field on the fundamental particles

source_refs.note: Topic 2.2, printed pages 24-25: the behaviour of the three particles in an electric field (Figure 2.1).

blocks.text: The behaviour of particles in an electric field depends upon their mass and charge. If we allow the beams of electrons, protons and neutrons to pass one by one at the same speed through an electric field, they show their behaviour as follows.

items: Neutrons being neutral are not deflected but travel in a straight path perpendicular to the direction of electric field.
Protons being positively charged are deflected towards the negative plate.
Electrons being negatively charged are deflected towards the positive plate, to greater extent since they are 1/1836 times lighter than protons.

blocks.alt: A beam of particles leaves a slit on the left and passes between two charged plates, the negative plate above and the positive plate below. The proton path p+ bends slightly up towards the negative plate, the neutron path n goes straight, and the electron path e- bends more strongly down towards the positive plate; the angle of deflection theta is marked between the n and e- paths.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.1: Behaviour of proton, electron and neutron in the electric field (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.1).

blocks.text: The amount of deviation from its original direction of movement is measured in two ways.
This is possible if we imagine that after deflection, the particle moves in a circular path. Hence, the factors affecting the radius of deflection are reciprocal to that for the angle of deflection.
